title: Fathers alleged to refute heretics from Church authority alone
source_text: XXIX. Denique, cum multi libri quorum authoritas semper certa fuit apud Orthodoxos, ab haereticis rejecti aut in dubium vocati sint, in eo multi sunt Pontificii, ut ostendant Patres refellisse illos haereticos ex authoritate, consensu, & testimonio Ecclesiae, quibus librorum istorum divinitatem & authoritatem vindicarunt & asseruerunt. Ita enim ex. gr. Augustinus loquitur de Actis Apostolorum, quorum authoritatem Manichaei negabant, Huic libro necesse est me credere, si credo Evangelio: cum utramque Scripturam pariter nobis Catholica commendet authoritas. Et adversus eosdem Manichaeos, Nostrorum, inquit, librorum authoritas tot gentium confessione, per successiones Apostolorum, Episcoporum, Conciliorumque roborata, vobis adversa est: Vestrorum autem nulla est, quae a tam paucis profertur, &c. Ex quibus & similibus concludunt Pontificii fidem nostram de Scriptura sacra ab Ecclesiae judicio pendere: ejusque authoritatem, testimonium & consensum esse regulam & amussim, ad quam Scriptura omnis probanda & examinanda est, ut certo de ea nobis constare possit: juxta celebre illud Augustini, Ego vero Evangelio non crederem nisi me Catholicae Ecclesiae commoveret authoritas. Et quod alibi dicit idem vir sanctus. Tenebit hunc modum fidelis animus in Scripturis Canonicis, ut eas quae ab omnibus accipiuntur Ecclesiis Catholicis praeponat eis quas quaedam non accipiunt. De iis vero quae non accipiuntur ab omnibus, praeferet eas quas plures gravioresque accipiunt, eis quas pauciores minorisque authoritatis Ecclesiae tenent.
pass_a_gloss: Finally, when many books whose authority was always certain among the Orthodox have been rejected or called into doubt by heretics, many Pontificals are intent on showing that the Fathers refuted those heretics from the authority, consent, and testimony of the Church, by which they vindicated and asserted the divinity and authority of those books. Thus for example Augustine speaks of the Acts of the Apostles, whose authority the Manichees denied: It is necessary that I believe this book if I believe the Gospel, since Catholic authority recommends both Scriptures equally to us. And against the same Manichees: The authority of our books, he says, strengthened by the confession of so many nations, through the successions of Apostles, Bishops, and Councils, is against you: but of yours there is none, which is put forward by so few, and so on. From which and similar things the Pontificals conclude that our faith concerning sacred Scripture depends on the Church's judgment; and that its authority, testimony, and consent are the rule and plumbline to which all Scripture is to be proved and examined, so that it can certainly be established for us concerning it — according to that famous saying of Augustine, But I would not believe the Gospel unless the authority of the Catholic Church moved me. And what the same holy man says elsewhere: The faithful mind will keep this measure in the Canonical Scriptures, that it prefer those which are received by all Catholic churches to those which some do not receive. But concerning those which are not received by all, it will prefer those which more and weightier churches receive to those which fewer churches of lesser authority hold.
pass_b_english: Finally, when heretics rejected or doubted many books whose authority was always sure among the Orthodox, many Roman doctors try to show that the Fathers refuted them from the Church's authority, consent, and testimony, by which they vindicated those books' divinity and authority.

So Augustine on Acts, which the Manichees denied: I must believe this book if I believe the Gospel, since Catholic authority recommends both Scriptures to us alike. And against the same: The authority of our books, strengthened by so many nations' confession through the successions of Apostles, bishops, and councils, stands against you; yours has none, being put forward by so few.

From this and the like they conclude that our faith about sacred Scripture hangs on the Church's judgment, and that its authority, testimony, and consent are the rule and plumbline by which all Scripture must be tested so we can be sure of it — citing Augustine's famous line, I would not believe the Gospel unless the Catholic Church's authority moved me.

And elsewhere the same holy man: The faithful mind will keep this measure in the Canonical Scriptures — prefer what all Catholic churches receive to what some refuse; and among books not received by all, prefer what more and weightier churches receive to what fewer churches of lesser standing hold.

lemmas.gloss: But I would not believe the Gospel

choices.why: Metaphor for the rule by which Scripture is tested.
